messages:
maria (support): Customer on private/VPC deploy (ACME) reporting failures when installer tries to pull model shards and contact model-registry. They have a corporate TLS-inspecting proxy. Error: TLS handshake fails or server cert shows corporate MITM cert.

kevin (eng-infra): Thanks — can you paste the exact curl output or installer log snippet? Also which installer version and model name?

maria (support): Installer v0.9.3, model: rw-large-v2. Log: 
```
2026-06-15T12:34:21Z error: download failed: https://model-registry.redwood.ai/shards/rw-large-v2/part-12 -> tls: remote error: tls: bad certificate
Caused by: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

liam (eng-ml): That looks like TLS interception. With our model registry we require SNI passthrough and OCSP/CRL checks to succeed. If the proxy terminates TLS, the client sees the proxy cert and verification fails against our CA.

maria (support): Customer also tried `curl -v` from a bastion and got this: 
```
$ curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/health
* Connected to model-registry.redwood.ai (3.35.120.88) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* TLS error: CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt function: X509_verify_cert error: self signed certificate in certificate chain
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
```

kevin (eng-infra): Ok. For on-prem installs behind TLS-inspecting proxies we recommend either: 
- Add exception/bypass for SNI hostnames we list below (no TLS interception), OR
- Install the corporate CA into the host truststore on your nodes (not ideal for managed installs).

kevin (eng-infra): Can you ask them to allow outbound to the following hosts/ports (SNI passthrough required):
- model-registry.redwood.ai :443 
- models.redwood.ai :443 
- auth.redwood.ai :443 (OAuth/JWKS)
- telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai :443 (if they want telemetry; installer can disable)
- pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org :443 (for pip deps)
- artifactory.redwood.ai :443 (private packages)
- docker.pkg.redwood.ai / registry-1.docker.io :443 (if using container pulls)
- ocsp.globalsign.com and crl.* hosts used for OCSP/CRL (allow outbound to common OCSP responders)

liam (eng-ml): Also note the model shard URLs may redirect to S3 or cloud storage buckets. Ask them to allow outbound to the cloud provider object store endpoints in their region (we'll include the exact redirect domains from logs if needed).

maria (support): They also reported a 403 from `https://auth.redwood.ai/token` when the installer tries to exchange the attestation. Snippet: 
```
POST /token 403 Forbidden
{"error":"invalid_client"}
```

kevin (eng-infra): 403 invalid_client usually means the POST body was altered by a proxy (e.g., changing headers or stripping TLS client certs). Ensure request body and Authorization headers are forwarded intact. If the proxy rewrites Host or injects headers, that can break our auth server validation.

maria (support): Customer asked for a minimal allowlist they can hand to security. Can we provide a copy-paste list they can give to firewall/proxy team?

kevin (eng-infra): Yep. Paste this to them and ask for SNI passthrough (no TLS inspection) for the listed hosts, allow outbound TCP 443. If they truly cannot disable inspection, they must install the corporate CA into every node truststore AND ensure OCSP passthrough works.

--- COPY-PASTE ALLOWLIST START ---
Hosts (SNI passthrough recommended):
- model-registry.redwood.ai:443
- models.redwood.ai:443
- auth.redwood.ai:443
- telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai:443
- artifactory.redwood.ai:443
- packages.redwood.ai (if used):443
- pypi.org:443
- files.pythonhosted.org:443
- registry-1.docker.io:443
- docker.pkg.redwood.ai:443
- ocsp.apple.com, ocsp.globalsign.com, ocsp.digicert.com:443
Cloud storage redirects (allow per-region object store endpoints if you see redirects):
- s3.amazonaws.com and regional S3 endpoints (if we redirect there)
- storage.googleapis.com (GCS)
Ports: 443 outbound TCP only
Notes:
- If a TLS-inspecting proxy is unavoidable, deploy the corporate CA to installed hosts' system truststore and ensure OCSP/CRL traffic is allowed so certificate revocation checks succeed.
- If security requires telemetry blocked, provide the installer flag `--disable-telemetry` (we can confirm version flag).
--- ALLOWLIST END ---

maria (support): I'll send this to customer. Anything else we should ask them to check?

liam (eng-ml): Ask them to capture a `tcpdump` of a failed handshake (pcap) and the curl `-v` output including the full certificate chain if they can. That helps us confirm whether our server cert never arrives.

kevin (eng-infra): Also confirm DNS resolves to public IPs (no internal split-horizon mapping to private IPs pointing at a corporate proxy). If they see internal IPs, we need to know what those map to.

maria (support): Thanks — sending now. Will escalate back here with their security team's response and any pcap. :pray:

deploy-bot: Installer v0.9.3 release notes: https://internal.redwood.dev/releases/0.9.3 (contains `--disable-telemetry` flag)

sre-oncall: Ping if they get stuck, we can schedule a quick remote session to validate TLS handshake with them.
